entries.title: HAI started
entries.note: Can a cheap model get measurably better at coding over time, without retraining, by remembering what worked and checking that memory against reality?
details: Coding first, because tests give a clear pass or fail. Without a reliable signal like that, an agent can't tell which of its lessons were right.

entries.title: Harness: fx, kept fixed
entries.note: fx is small, scriptable and embeddable, which makes it easy to run thousands of tasks. The harness itself won't be self-edited.
details: fx is written in Zig, so a self-edit would mean a compile step that can fail. Self-improvement happens in a layer of prompts, skills and tools on top, versioned in git and easy to roll back.

entries.title: Model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through the OpenCode API
entries.note: Strong on coding benchmarks and very cheap to run, which matters when every experiment means hundreds of tasks.
details: Its weights are open, but at 552B total parameters it isn't practical to fine-tune at home. Weight updates move to a separate stage with a small local model.

entries.title: Memory should be code, not just notes
entries.note: A memory stored as a test or probe can be run before it's trusted, and retired when it starts failing. Added as its own stage to compare against prose memory.
details: Prose memories go stale silently. Runnable ones tell you when they've stopped being true.

entries.title: How progress will be measured
entries.note: Ordered task stream; every 25 tasks, a score on held-out tasks with memory frozen. Tracked: pass rate, regressions, steps per solved task, memory size.
details: Stopping rule, set in advance: if memory doesn't add at least 3–5 points on held-out tasks after about 200 tasks, the core idea is weak.

entries.title: Expect small gains from memory alone
entries.note: Google's ReasoningBank added 4.6 points on SWE-Bench Verified. SICA's self-edits went from 17% to 53%, but with frontier models doing the reflecting.
details: If HAI matches the first, memory is worth keeping. The bigger question is whether executable memory and strategy edits add more on top.

next.title: Run the baseline
next.note: fx and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with no memory, on the first 100 tasks, three times each. This sets the starting score and shows how noisy runs are.
